cues.text: Hello, Helen. Sorry I’m late.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Hi, Jeremy, no problem. Well we’d better work out where we are on our project, I suppose.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Yeah. I’ve looked at the drawings you’ve done for my story, ‘The Forest’, and I think they’re brilliant – they really create the atmosphere I had in mind when I was writing it.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: I’m glad you like them.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: There are just a few suggestions I’d like to make.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Go ahead.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Now, I’m not sure about the drawing of the cave – it’s got trees all around it, which is great, but the drawing’s a bit too static, isn’t it? I think it needs some action.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Yes, there’s nothing happening. Perhaps I should add the boy – Malcolm, isn’t it? He would be walking up to it.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Yes, let’s have Malcolm in the drawing. And what about putting in a tiger – the one that he makes friends with a bit later? Maybe it could be sitting under a tree washing itself.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: And the tiger stops in the middle of what it’s doing when it sees Malcolm walking past.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: That’s a good idea.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: OK, I’ll have a go at that.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Then there’s the drawing of the crowd of men and women dancing. They’re just outside the forest, and there’s a lot going on.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: That’s right, you wanted them to be watching a carnival procession, but I thought it would be too crowded. Do you think it works like this?
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Yes, I like what you’ve done. The only thing is, could you add Malcolm to it, without changing what’s already there.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: What about having him sitting on the tree trunk on the right of the picture?
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Yes, that would be fine.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: And do you want him watching the other people?
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: No, he’s been left out of all the fun, so I’d like him to be crying – that’ll contrast nicely with the next picture, where he’s laughing at the clowns in the carnival.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Right, I’ll do that.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: And then the drawing of the people ice skating in the forest.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: I wasn’t too happy with that one. Because they’re supposed to be skating on grass aren’t they?
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: That’s right, and it’s frozen over. At the moment it doesn’t look quite right.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Mm, I see what you mean. I’ll have another go at that.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: And I like the wool hats they’re wearing. Maybe you could give each of them a scarf as well.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Yeah, that’s easy enough. They can be streaming out behind the people to suggest they’re skating really fast.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Mm, great. Well that’s all on the drawings.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Right. So you’ve finished writing your story and I just need to finish illustrating it, and my story and your drawings are done.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: So the next thing is to decide what exactly we need to write about in the report that goes with the stories, and how we’re going to divide the work.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Right, Helen.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: What do you think about including a section on how we planned the project as a whole, Jeremy? That’s probably quite important.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Yeah. Well, you’ve had most of the good ideas so far. How do you feel about drafting something, then we can go through it together and discuss it?
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: OK, that seems reasonable. And I could include something on how we came up with the ideas for our two stories, couldn’t I?
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: Well, I’ve started writing something about that, so why don’t you do the same and we can include the two things.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Right. So what about our interpretation of the stories? Do we need to write about what we think they show, like the value of helping other people, all that sort of thing?
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: That’s going to come up later isn’t it? I think everyone in the class is going to read each other’s stories and come up with their own interpretations which we’re going to discuss.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Oh, I missed that. So it isn’t going to be part of the report at all?
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: No. But we need to write about the illustrations, because they’re an essential element of children’s experience of reading the stories. It’s probably easiest for you to write that section, as you know more about drawing than I do.
cues.speaker: JEREMY

cues.text: Maybe, but I find it quite hard to write about. I’d be happier if you did it.
cues.speaker: HELEN

cues.text: OK. So when do you think …
cues.speaker: JEREMY
